# Contract review

A contract the company is about to sign, reviewed by legal (fictional rules): the agent summarizes it for the reviewers, a lawyer of the legal team takes it in and names the reviewer, two lawyers review a contract over 5,000,000 yen, and the general counsel decides one over 10,000,000 yen

File: `contract.ringi` (the request `contract`, version 1, sha256:ae57995cfb44cd30).

Kept by the team Legal (`legal`).

The organization is read in its version in effect on 2026-11-16: the one from 2026-04-01.

## When it can be used

- From 2026-04-01: the first version of the organization `shared/company.ringi` (data `../org`).
- With no end: nothing it reads ends.

## Who may submit it

Everyone in the organization may submit it.

In numbers: 24 of 24 people in the organization from 2026-04-01.

A person may also submit it in the name of someone they stand in for (a proxy for submitting): the request is then that person's.

## Form

| Field | Type | Accepts | Required | Shown |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Counterparty | text, one line | 1 to 100 characters | yes | always |
| Kind of contract | one of Non-disclosure agreement, Service agreement or License agreement | — | yes | always |
| Contract value | amount in JPY | from 0 JPY to 1,000,000,000 JPY | yes | always |
| Term in months | number | from 1 to 60 | yes | always |
| Contract | a file | — | yes | always |
| Text of the contract | text | 1 to 20,000 characters | yes | always |
| Reviewer | a person of the organization | — | filled in by an approver | always |
| Risks legal notes | text | up to 2000 characters | filled in by an approver, optional | when “Kind of contract” is not “Non-disclosure agreement” |

> A field left empty has no value: one that is optional, one asked for or shown on a condition, and one an approver fills in, until they do. A condition that a field “is not” a value holds when it has no value; one that it “is” a value, or that compares it, does not. A computation that reads a field with no value has none either, but a total, which adds the rows whose cell is filled in.

## Route

The stages, in order. A stage with a condition comes only where it holds; who answers each stage is said under “How the approvers are chosen”.

| Stage | Who answers | When it comes |
|---|---|---|
| manager | manager | always |
| summary | a summary the flow `summarize` writes | always |
| intake | legal | always |
| review | reviewer | always |
| second | at least 2 of legal | when “Contract value” is more than 5,000,000 JPY |
| counsel | counsel | when “Contract value” is more than 10,000,000 JPY |
| finance | circulated to finance | when “Kind of contract” is “License agreement” |

## How the approvers are chosen

| Approver | Who it is |
|---|---|
| manager | the requester's manager: the head of the team the requester is mainly in, or of the team above where that head is the requester or there is none |
| legal | the members of the team Legal (`legal`): one of them answers |
| reviewer | the person the approver of the stage before enters in “Reviewer” |
| counsel | e9001 (General counsel), always this person |
| finance | the members of the team Finance (`finance`): one of them answers |

Each approver is chosen when the stage starts, in the version of the organization in effect then. A proxy in effect that day answers beside them (see “Proxies”).

## Deadlines and reminders

Every stage:

- It is due 3 business days after it starts, at the end of the day.
- Its approvers are reminded 2 business days after it starts, at 09:00.
- When it is late, it goes up to the head above, and its deadline is counted again from then; when it is late again, the ticket expires.
- When nobody can answer it, it waits for an administrator to add an approver.

The stage “manager”, in place of those:

- When nobody can answer it, it goes up to the head above; at the top of the organization, the stage is skipped.

The stage “counsel”, in place of those:

- When nobody can answer it, it goes up to the head above; at the top of the organization, it waits for an administrator.

For a stage that starts on 2026-04-03 (Fri), the days the request's calendar closes skipped (times in UTC+09:00):

A ticket ends within 192 business days at the most (4 × 38 at its stages, 3 × 10 with the requester, 10 paused). `ritsu ringi doc --longest` shows the dates of the longest.

## Rules of a ticket

- A requester does not approve their own request: they are left out of the approvers of every stage, and so is the one who submitted it in their name.
- An approver may send it back to the requester, or to an earlier stage that has answered, at most 3 times in all, withdrawals counted. After that, they approve or reject it.
- Sent back to the requester, it may be submitted again until the end of the day 10 business days after; then it expires. Only the fields that change are given again.
- The requester may withdraw it until the stage “counsel” answers. Withdrawn, it comes back to them, to be submitted again or dropped.
- An approver may pause the ticket, 10 business days in all: its reminders and deadline stop, and move later by the days it was paused. When the days run out, it goes on by itself.
- Approvers may correct “Risks legal notes” and “Reviewer”.
- An approver may reject it: it ends rejected, and cannot be submitted again.
- The team that keeps the request may add an approver to the stage a ticket is at, and hand one approver's part over to someone else. Neither moves a deadline.

## Comments

- A person may add a comment to what they do (submitting, approving, sending back, rejecting, withdrawing and the others), or write one on its own. One with no comment is the same as one with an empty comment.
- Who may write one is decided by the gate `shared/company.gate`, as for the other operations.
- A comment is up to 2000 characters. It is kept in the ticket's history, on the line of what the person did, with who wrote it and when, and is not changed after. Writing one on its own changes neither the state of the ticket nor its deadlines.
- An approver may reject or send back a request without a reason, but a reason written tells the requester what to correct.

## Proxies

- A proxy for approving answers the stages of the person they stand in for, beside them, on the days the row says. Their answer counts once, in that person's seat. They may also pause and resume, correct the fields approvers correct, and retract an approval they gave.
- A proxy for submitting submits requests in the name of the person they stand in for, and may withdraw, submit again and drop them as the requester does.
- Whatever a proxy does is kept in the history with whose place they did it in.

The organization's data has no proxy for this request.

## Books and flows

The request holds nothing in a book and starts no flow when it is submitted or ends.

## Claims

The check holds each of these: a claim that did not hold would stop the request.

- `counsel_decides_large_contracts`: the stage “counsel” is “counsel” only when “Contract value” is more than 10,000,000 JPY.
- `ends_in_time`: every ticket ends within 192 business days; at the most it takes 192.
